findings.text: In Rom 8:5 and Rom 8:6 the mind is set on something: a person directs his mind to an object and holds it there, so that the mind-set becomes his frame of thought. It is stated as done by those who live one way or the other.

parts.grounds: set their minds on the things of the Spirit

findings.text: In Rom 8:5 and Rom 8:6 what the mind is set on is one of two opposites: the flesh and its things, or the Spirit and its things.

parts.grounds: set the mind on the flesh

findings.text: In Rom 8:5 the way a person lives, by the flesh or by the Spirit, goes with where the mind is set, and in Rom 8:6 the set of mind is itself death, or life and peace: living, the set of mind and its outcome are joined.
In Rom 8:5 and Rom 8:6 the setting of the mind is a pursuit of its object, in either direction: toward the flesh or toward the Spirit.

parts.grounds: those who live according to the Spirit
